about.title: Madera Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a loved one on a Madera road changes everything, often in an instant and without warning. Madera County sees its share of collisions along corridors like Rt 145, Cleveland Avenue W, Tozer Street, and Cleveland Avenue, and with 3 traffic deaths recorded in the most recent final crash year, families across the city have faced this exact kind of loss. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim. These claims can address funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. It's a civil matter separate from any criminal proceeding tied to the crash. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply help Madera families reach an independent attorney who can walk through what's possible, with no upfront cost and no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, typically starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents or heirs. An attorney can help clarify where your family stands under this order.

items.title: A Firm Deadline That Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity is involved. Waiting to speak with someone can cost you options.

items.title: Losses That Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law recognizes more than just funeral and burial costs, it also accounts for lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a family has been deprived of. An independent attorney can help you understand what applies to your situation.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Madera?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If a government agency or public roadway maintenance issue is involved, that deadline can be much shorter, so it's worth speaking with an attorney early rather than waiting.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring this kind of claim?
items.answer: California law prioritizes a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children as the first in line to file. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An attorney can look at your family's specific circumstances and explain where you fit.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a road like Cleveland Avenue in Madera?
items.answer: The specific road doesn't change your legal rights, but knowing where a crash occurred can help an attorney understand the circumstances and gather relevant records. Madera's higher-traffic corridors, including Rt 145 and Cleveland Avenue, are simply part of the factual picture an attorney would look into.

items.question: What kinds of losses can a wrongful death claim cover?
items.answer: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. These are meant to reflect both the financial and personal impact of the loss on surviving family members.
